findings.title: Match statistics write is rolled back for blocked emails when it runs inside User#save
findings.body: `should_block?` updates and saves `match_count` and `last_match_at` while the User model is validating. `User#save` runs validations inside its own transaction. When the email is blocked, validation fails, `save` returns false, and Rails raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, which also rolls back the BlockedEmail update. As a result, blocked attempts that go through `user.save` alone (e.g. when `call_discourse_hub` is off) are never recorded. Those are exactly the hits the statistics are meant to capture. Only the separate `user.valid?` call in the controller, which runs outside a transaction, persists the count. The specs miss this because they call `should_block?` directly. Recording the match outside the validation transaction, or not in a validator at all, would fix it.

findings.title: Validation runs twice per signup, double-counting BlockedEmail matches
findings.body: `create` calls `user.valid?` (when `call_discourse_hub` is on) and then `user.save`, which validates again. Validation now has a side effect: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves. A matching `do_nothing` entry, whose save succeeds and is not rolled back, is therefore counted twice per signup attempt. Any other code path that calls `valid?` before `save` inflates the counter the same way. Keeping side effects out of validators avoids this.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized, so the block is easy to bypass
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact, case-sensitive match on whatever the user typed. Neither the stored value nor the input is downcased or stripped. If `block@spamfromhome.org` is blocked, a spammer can register as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` or with surrounding whitespace and pass validation. Normalize both sides, for example with `Email.downcase(...).strip` on save and on lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write increment of match_count
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads the row, increments it in Ruby, and writes it back. Concurrent signup attempts with the same email can each read the same value, and the later write overwrites the earlier one, losing increments. Each save also runs the uniqueness validation query. An atomic `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` avoids both problems.

findings.title: Any server-side email rejection is shown inline as 'invalid email'
findings.body: The client adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present. That includes 'has already been taken', the domain whitelist/blacklist message, and 'is not allowed'. The inline reason is then always `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`. A user whose correctly formatted address is already registered sees a 'please enter a valid email' hint that contradicts the flash error. The message should reflect the server's actual error, e.g. using `result.errors.email`.
